key_insight: This paper extends social laws from deterministic, goal-driven multi-agent systems to stochastic, reward-based environments. It introduces a formal way to check whether coordination rules remain effective when outcomes are uncertain.
problem_solved: Multi-agent systems often suffer from interference between agents, especially when the environment is stochastic and rewards are uncertain. Existing social-law methods were mostly designed for deterministic settings, leaving a gap for robust coordination in real-world noisy environments.
method: Define social laws for stochastic, reward-based multi-agent settings instead of only deterministic goal-based ones.
Introduce α-robustness as a formal measure of how reliably a social law preserves good individual performance under uncertainty.
Provide a framework for verifying whether a proposed social law remains robust across different environment conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a principled way to design coordination rules that are less brittle in noisy, real-world multi-agent systems. It can help improve safety, reliability, and performance when multiple agents must act without interfering with one another.
visual_elements: A side-by-side comparison of deterministic vs. stochastic multi-agent environments
A flow diagram showing agents, social laws, and outcome verification
A robustness curve or heatmap illustrating α-robustness under increasing uncertainty
Icons for agents, rewards, randomness, and interference prevention
paper_title: Social Laws for Multi-agent Coordination in Stochastic Environments
paper_authors: Rolando Fernandez, Caleb Probine, Tyler Lee, Jeffrey Chen, Erez Karpas
